notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0096.stoa003.opp-la: Section III is an acrostic: the first letters spell CVLTVRA DAEMONVM, lost in English. ‘Cum- m Deus /’ (1.3.1) is read as Cum Deus, and ‘in term’ (1.3.9) as in terra. The sense of 1.3.11 (Mortales et illi mortuos simulacro ponebant) is uncertain.

nodes.text: if empty idols are abandoned and are not worshipped.
When God almighty had adorned the nature of the world,
he wished this earth to be visited by angels;
his laws they, once sent down, despised;
so great was the beauty of women that it turned them aside.
Since, defiled, they cannot return to heaven,
rebels from then on, they hurled words against God.
Thereupon the Most High sent his sentence upon them;
from their seed the Giants are said to have been born.
By them arts were brought forth on earth,
and they taught the dyeing of wool and everything that is done;
They too were mortal, and set up the dead as images.
But the Almighty, because they were of a depraved seed,
did not decree that, once dead, they be taken back from death.
Hence now, wandering, they overthrow many bodies;
it is chiefly they whom today you worship and pray to as gods.
And Saturn the old man, if a god: when does a god grow old?
